children: Canada video networking firm's fiscal Q3 revenue declined 1.4% yr/yr, slightly beating analyst expectations
Adjusted EBITDA for fiscal Q3 dropped sharply, impacted by lower gross margins and higher expenses
Company says revenue decline tied to timing of customer purchasing and deployment cycles in Broadcast segment
Haivision says customer demand remains strong but notes extended procurement cycles may shift revenue timing
Company expects near-term margin compression due to supply chain challenges and tariffs
Haivision sees healthy demand for secure, high-quality video solutions in enterprise and broadcast markets
PURCHASING CYCLES - Co said revenue decline was due to timing of customer purchasing and deployment cycles, particularly in Broadcast segment
SUPPLY CHAIN COSTS - Gross margins were impacted by supply-chain challenges and input costs rising faster than price adjustments, per CFO Dan Rabinowitz
DISCIPLINED CUSTOMER SPENDING - Co said broadcast technology customers are showing more disciplined purchasing behavior, focusing on returns and efficiency
*Applies to a deviation of less than 1%; not applicable for per-share numbers.
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 4 "strong buy" or "buy", no "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the integrated hardware & software peer group is "buy"
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Haivision Systems Inc is C$7.75, about 81.5% above its September 8 closing price of C$4.27
The stock recently traded at 27 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 24 three months ago
